text:
Abstract

According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Aero Engine Coatings market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.

The global Aero Engine Coatings market is projected to experience significant transformation and expansion from 2026 to 2035, underpinned by the aerospace industry's relentless pursuit of efficiency, durability, and reduced emissions. This specialized, high-performance segment encompasses critical technologies like Thermal Barrier Coatings (TBCs) and Environmental Barrier Coatings (EBCs), which are essential for protecting engine components from extreme temperatures, corrosion, and wear. Growth will be fundamentally driven by two parallel forces: the introduction of new, more fuel-efficient engine platforms with higher operating temperatures from OEMs like GE Aerospace, Rolls-Royce, and Pratt & Whitney, and the sustained demand from the massive global fleet Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) sector. The market's trajectory is further shaped by the gradual fleet renewal towards new-generation aircraft, stringent environmental regulations pushing for longer service intervals and better performance, and the expanding application of industrial gas turbines for power generation. However, this growth is tempered by challenges including the high cost and complexity of advanced coating application, lengthy qualification cycles, and competitive pressure from aftermarket alternatives. This analysis provides a comprehensive outlook on the demand drivers, key end-use sectors, regional dynamics, and competitive landscape defining the market's path through 2035.

The baseline scenario for the Aero Engine Coatings market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates steady, technology-driven growth, with the market's value compound annual growth rate (CAGR) reflecting the underlying health of the global aviation and energy sectors. The fundamental demand floor is supported by the continuous MRO cycle of the existing global fleet, which requires coating refurbishment during engine overhauls. This aftermarket segment provides consistent, recurring revenue. The primary growth vector stems from the adoption of new engine programs, such as the GE9X, Rolls-Royce UltraFan, and Pratt & Whitney GTF families, which utilize more advanced, multi-layer coating systems to achieve higher thermal efficiency and meet stricter emission standards. The market will see a gradual shift in product mix towards higher-value ceramic-based and nanocomposite coatings. Geographically, Asia-Pacific will consolidate its position as the dominant region, fueled by its large and growing commercial fleet, expanding MRO capabilities, and increasing aircraft production. North America and Europe will remain critical as centers for R&D, OEM production, and high-value military applications. The market's expansion will be moderated by the high barriers to entry, the capital-intensive nature of coating application technology, and the intense scrutiny from aviation authorities, ensuring that growth is coupled with an unwavering focus on quality, certification, and performance validation.

Demand Drivers and Constraints

Primary Demand Drivers

Accelerated adoption of next-generation, fuel-efficient jet engines requiring advanced thermal management

Stringent global emissions regulations (e.g., ICAO CAEP) pushing for extended engine on-wing time and efficiency

Rising global air passenger traffic and fleet expansion, particularly in Asia-Pacific and Middle East

Increasing demand for MRO services as the global aircraft fleet ages, driving recoating cycles

Growth in industrial gas turbine installations for power generation, requiring protective coatings

Military modernization programs investing in high-performance engines for next-gen fighter jets and helicopters

Potential Growth Constraints

Exceptionally high cost and lengthy qualification processes for new coating materials and processes

Technical complexity and capital intensity of coating application equipment (e.g., EB-PVD, plasma spray)

Intense competitive pressure and margin erosion in the aftermarket segment from alternative suppliers

Vulnerability to cyclical downturns in the commercial aviation and energy sectors

Stringent and evolving environmental, health, and safety regulations governing coating materials and processes

Demand Structure by End-Use Industry

Commercial Aviation (Turbofans) (estimated share: 45%)

This segment is the largest and most dynamic, driven by the dual engines of new aircraft production and a vast, aging fleet requiring maintenance. Demand is directly tied to aircraft deliveries of next-generation models (A320neo, 737 MAX, 787, A350) whose engines operate at higher pressures and temperatures, mandating more sophisticated TBCs and EBCs. Concurrently, the existing fleet of over 25,000 commercial jets undergoes mandatory shop visits every 5-7 years, where worn coatings are stripped and reapplied. Key demand-side indicators include annual aircraft delivery rates, global Revenue Passenger Kilometers (RPK), and average fleet age. Through 2035, the trend towards more durable coatings that extend time-on-wing will be paramount, as airlines seek to reduce maintenance downtime and costs. The rise of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) compatibility may also introduce new material compatibility requirements for coatings. Current trend: Strong Growth.

Major trends: Shift towards ceramic matrix composite (CMC) components in hot sections, requiring advanced EBCs, Development of 'CMAS-resistant' TBCs to mitigate degradation from airborne sand and dust, Integration of coating health monitoring sensors within engine control systems, and Growing emphasis on coatings that enable higher turbine inlet temperatures for improved fuel burn.

Representative participants: GE Aerospace, Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney, Safran, MTU Aero Engines, and CFM International.

Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul (MRO) (estimated share: 30%)

The MRO segment provides a consistent, recurring demand base largely insulated from new production cycles. It is a service-driven market where coating application is a critical step in engine overhaul. Demand is mechanistic: as engines accumulate flight cycles and hours, their protective coatings degrade and must be refurbished to restore performance and meet OEM specifications. The demand story is tied to the size, age, and utilization rate of the global fleet. An older fleet increases shop visit intensity. Key indicators include global MRO market size, engine shop visit forecasts, and airline operating expenditures. Through 2035, this segment will see growth from fleet expansion and aging, but also face pressure from OEMs and airlines seeking longer intervals between overhauls via more durable coatings. The competitive landscape is intense, with airlines and MRO providers constantly balancing OEM-specified coatings against qualified, lower-cost alternatives. Current trend: Stable Growth.

Major trends: Expansion of independent MRO networks in Asia-Pacific and Middle East challenging OEM service centers, Adoption of advanced stripping and reapplication techniques to reduce turnaround time, Increasing use of data analytics to predict optimal coating refurbishment timing, and Growth in 'power-by-the-hour' contracts that transfer coating maintenance risk to OEMs/MROs.

Representative participants: Lufthansa Technik, ST Engineering, Delta TechOps, HAECO, AAR Corp, and SIA Engineering.

Military Aviation (estimated share: 15%)

Military engine coatings demand is driven by modernization programs, operational tempo, and the need for extreme performance and durability. Unlike commercial engines, military engines (for fighter jets, transports, helicopters) face more severe thermal cycling, higher thrust-to-weight requirements, and potential ingestion of abrasive materials. This necessitates highly specialized, often proprietary, coating systems. Demand is linked to defense budgets, new aircraft program timelines (e.g., F-35, NGAD, Tempest), and fleet refurbishment cycles. Key indicators include defense procurement spending on aircraft and engine upgrades. Through 2035, demand will be supported by global geopolitical tensions driving fleet upgrades, with a focus on stealth characteristics, extended range, and enhanced durability in harsh environments. The segment is characterized by stringent performance specifications, lower volume but higher value per unit, and a supply chain deeply integrated with national defense priorities. Current trend: Moderate Growth.

Major trends: Development of low-observable (stealth) coatings for engine components to reduce radar signature, Focus on coatings for high-Mach number applications and variable cycle engines, Increased use of additive manufacturing for engine parts, requiring compatible coating solutions, and Modernization of legacy fleets (F-16, F-15, Apache) with upgraded engine coatings.

Representative participants: Pratt & Whitney (Military Engines), GE Aerospace (Defense), Rolls-Royce (Defense), Safran (Defense), and Honeywell Aerospace.

Industrial Gas Turbines (Power Generation) (estimated share: 7%)

This segment serves gas turbines used for electricity generation and mechanical drive applications. Demand is driven by the global shift towards natural gas as a transition fuel and the need for flexible, rapid-response power generation to complement renewables. IGTs operate for thousands of hours under high temperatures and pressures, requiring robust TBCs and corrosion-resistant coatings to ensure efficiency and longevity. The demand mechanism is tied to new turbine installations, especially in emerging markets for base-load power, and the maintenance cycle of the installed base. Key indicators include global investments in gas-fired power plants, capacity additions, and natural gas price stability. Through 2035, demand will be supported by energy security concerns and grid modernization, with an emphasis on coatings that improve efficiency, allow for fuel flexibility (including hydrogen blends), and reduce maintenance frequency in both heavy-duty and aeroderivative turbines. Current trend: Steady Growth.

Major trends: Coatings development for hydrogen and hydrogen-blend capable turbines to reduce carbon emissions, Demand for retrofit coatings to upgrade the efficiency of existing turbine fleets, Growth in aeroderivative gas turbines for peaking power, leveraging aerospace coating technology, and Increasing operating temperatures in advanced combined-cycle plants to boost efficiency.

Representative participants: GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Power, Ansaldo Energia, and Kawasaki Heavy Industries.

Helicopter & Auxiliary Power Units (APUs) (estimated share: 3%)

This niche segment encompasses turboshaft engines for helicopters and small gas turbines used as APUs on aircraft. Demand is driven by the operational needs of offshore oil & gas, emergency medical services, search and rescue, and business aviation. Helicopter engines, in particular, face challenging environments with high levels of dust, sand, and salt, necessitating robust erosion and corrosion protection. The demand story is linked to helicopter deliveries, the health of the offshore industry, and the fleet of wide-body aircraft requiring APU services. Key indicators include civil helicopter production rates and aftermarket support activity. Through 2035, growth will be steady but modest, focused on enhancing durability in harsh environments and improving the performance of new, more efficient turboshaft and APU designs. The segment is characterized by specialized, lower-volume coating solutions tailored to specific engine models and operating conditions. Current trend: Niche Growth.

Major trends: Focus on erosion-resistant coatings for engines operating in desert and maritime environments, Development of coatings for new, more fuel-efficient turboshaft engine designs, MRO demand driven by high utilization in emergency service and utility helicopter fleets, and Lightweight coating solutions for APUs to minimize aircraft weight.

Representative participants: Safran Helicopter Engines, GE Aerospace (T700/CT7 series), Pratt & Whitney Canada, Honeywell (APUs), and Rolls-Royce (M250, RR300).

Key Market Participants

Regional Dynamics

Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 38%)

Asia-Pacific is the epicenter of market growth, driven by massive fleet expansion in China and India, burgeoning low-cost carrier sectors, and the region's establishment as a global MRO hub (Singapore, China, UAE). Rising aircraft production, particularly in China, further integrates coating demand into the regional supply chain. This region will see the highest CAGR through 2035. Direction: Dominant and Fastest Growing.

North America (estimated share: 28%)

North America remains a critical market anchored by the presence of major engine OEMs (GE, Pratt & Whitney), a large, mature airline fleet, and leading MRO providers. Demand is driven by technological innovation, military spending, and the need to maintain the world's largest commercial fleet. Growth will be steady, tied to OEM R&D and fleet renewal cycles. Direction: Mature Innovation Center.

Europe (estimated share: 22%)

Europe is a key market supported by strong OEMs (Rolls-Royce, Safran, MTU), a robust aviation network, and stringent environmental regulations pushing for efficient engine technologies. Demand is balanced between new engine programs (e.g., UltraFan) and a significant MRO base. Growth is linked to aerospace investment and the region's decarbonization agenda. Direction: Steady with Focus on Technology.

Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 8%)

The Middle East, in particular, is a strategic hub for long-haul aviation and premium MRO services, driving demand for high-performance coatings. The region's harsh operating environment necessitates frequent coating refurbishment. Africa presents smaller, fragmented growth opportunities linked to fleet modernization and resource extraction activities. Direction: Strategic Niche Growth.

Latin America (estimated share: 4%)

Latin America represents a smaller market with growth potential tied to economic recovery and fleet renewal among regional carriers. The coastal and tropical environment drives specific corrosion-related coating needs. Market development is slower, constrained by economic volatility and infrastructure challenges, but MRO activities provide a stable demand base. Direction: Modest Recovery and Growth.

Market Outlook (2026-2035)

In the baseline scenario, IndexBox estimates a 5.8% compound annual growth rate for the global aero engine coatings market over 2026-2035, bringing the market index to roughly 178 by 2035 (2025=100).

Note: indexed curves are used to compare medium-term scenario trajectories when full absolute volumes are not publicly disclosed.

title: The Iran war is reshaping global aviation - The Business Times
description:
That dynamic changed almost overnight when the Iran war broke out, shuttering airspaces, grounding planes and leaving regional airlines in disarray.
For European carriers trying to steal a march on rivals, another challenge is surging fuel prices as the war disrupts energy markets.
The Middle East airlines “won’t have shelved their ambitions to be global hubs”, said Rob Walker, an aviation analyst at consultancy ICF.
The longer the war persists, the worse it will be for the carriers with bases in the Middle East.
Morgan Stanley and UBS recently cut share-price targets on a number of European airlines, citing fuel costs.
text:
[LONDON] For years, airlines in the US and Europe have gawked at the rise of Middle East carriers funnelling ever more passengers through their gleaming hubs in Dubai and Doha at competitive prices with the latest jets.

Emirates, Qatar Airways and Etihad Airways offered a viable alternative in the Gulf, leveraging a perfect position between three continents – Europe, Africa and Asia.

That dynamic changed almost overnight when the Iran war broke out, shuttering airspaces, grounding planes and leaving regional airlines in disarray. While the loss of capacity from the Middle Eastern carriers has reduced long-haul flying overall, Western airlines are moving in to fill the gap.

Executives have sensed an opportunity to take advantage and regain ground, adding alternative routes to steal away business. Deutsche Lufthansa, British Airways and Air France-KLM quickly redeployed jets into countries including India, Thailand and Singapore last month to capture passengers looking for new flights. The gains in share are small so far, however, and building something with lasting momentum is not simple.

Bloomberg analysed widebody flights across 21 major airlines in the month before and after the war began, using data from tracking firm Flightradar24.(1)

One issue will be whether this is a short-term blip for global air travel or prove to be a more lasting change as places once considered safe are tainted with the long shadow of war.

For European carriers trying to steal a march on rivals, another challenge is surging fuel prices as the war disrupts energy markets. That means either fare hikes or absorbing those costs to lure in new customers, with little sense of how long the conflict will continue.

The Middle East airlines “won’t have shelved their ambitions to be global hubs”, said Rob Walker, an aviation analyst at consultancy ICF. “The Europeans, they’ve just got to try and make hay while the sun is shining.”

So far, the big increase in flight capacity has been in the US, though that reflects plans that were in motion before the Middle East disruption.

The biggest carriers, such as United Airlines and Delta Air Lines have expanded long-haul widebody flying by 11 per cent and 12 per cent, respectively, according to tracker Flightradar24. They added flights to existing destinations in Europe, as well as new routes to cater to well-heeled American tourists.

Jet fuel

US airlines are more exposed to surges in jet fuel prices as they are not hedged, though they enjoyed a bump in demand last month as passengers pounced to book before those costs pushed up fares.

On the Middle East disruption, nonstop flights from the US to Asia will benefit, as will transatlantic routes where US airlines code-share with European carriers, according to Walker.

The longer the war persists, the worse it will be for the carriers with bases in the Middle East. US President Donald Trump this week remained vague on the timeline of the war and pledged more aggressive actions against Iran.

Given its geographical advantage, Turkish Airlines also gained market share in the month after the war began, while Qatar Airways lost the most, according to the data analysed by Bloomberg.

Lufthansa saw a pickup in short-term demand, but wants to make these new route switches more permanent. Chief financial officer Till Streichert said there is “absolutely” the potential to move capacity to Asia on a more lasting basis.

Such moves are not always straightforward, particularly if there is an aircraft mismatch. A single-aisle jet serving a European-Gulf route will not necessarily be suitable for a longer-haul trip to Asia, and new, fuel-efficient widebody aircraft have years-long waiting lists. Plus, opening new routes takes months of preparation involving landing slots, schedules and staffing.

Meanwhile, worries about a jet fuel shortage have prompted Lufthansa management to ready crisis plans that could involve grounding planes.

Lufthansa shares are down 17 per cent since the war began. British Airways parent IAG has fallen 13 per cent in the same period, while Air France-KLM has dropped 27 per cent. Morgan Stanley and UBS recently cut share-price targets on a number of European airlines, citing fuel costs.

Price war

While the end of the war remains unclear, what’s certain is that the Mideast carriers will return to the market hungry to regain ground, and pricing could come into play.

“I would expect the Gulf carriers to offer highly attractive fares to rebuild traffic via their hubs, so maybe the European carriers will only have a short window of opportunity to exploit high demand and high fares,” said Richard Evans, senior consultant at analytics firm Cirium.

The Middle East hub model saw Emirates and Etihad enjoy massive growth in recent decades. Emirates carried 55.6 million passengers in 2025, more than quadruple the number ferried just 20 years earlier.

That helped to make Dubai the world’s busiest international airport, but rivals say the airlines’ expansion was for years sustained by unfair subsidies.

“It drives me crazy when people say, ‘These Gulf carriers are so amazing, they’ve got brand-new airplanes, they’ve got fantastic new airports’,” Air France-KLM CEO Ben Smith said in an interview last month. “But when you’re in an unlevel playing field, you can produce that.”

Asian airlines have boosted their long-haul trips too, with Singapore Airlines adding services to London and Melbourne, while Hong Kong’s Cathay Pacific Airways ramped up flights to Paris, Zurich and London. Air India said it has introduced more services and Australia’s Qantas Airways is also trying to add capacity on European routes.

Flying between Asia and Europe was already tricky because many Western airlines were forced to dodge Russian airspace following its invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The Iran conflict has exacerbated that. With Iranian and Iraqi airspaces closed, aircraft are being routed through narrow strips over Georgia, Azerbaijan and central Asia.

“The issue for European carriers to Asia is airspace availability, and competing with Asian airlines that are more competitive and can fly over Russia,” said Conroy Gaynor, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. “We think more capacity will end up on the Atlantic but have concerns on whether there is enough demand to absorb a significant increase.” BLOOMBERG

title: Brazil Air Travel Costs Surge in 2026 as Jet Fuel Hike Forces Higher Airfares and Shifts Travel Plans
description:
In early April 2026, Petrobras — Brazil’s state‑controlled oil producer — confirmed a 54.8% increase in the price of jet fuel sold to distributors.
This spike comes amid elevated global energy prices and geopolitical tensions, pushing aviation fuel costs sharply upward.
Proposals include temporary reductions in certain federal fuel taxes and expedited refunds of state levies on aviation fuel.
Consumer Tips on Navigating the New Pricing Climate In this era of elevated jet fuel prices, travellers can take steps to navigate the situation effectively.
In Brazil, the jet fuel price hike highlights how macroeconomic and energy sector decisions directly influence the travel experience.
text:
Travel budgets and flight costs in Brazil are facing a significant shake‑up in 2026 as the nation’s oil giant Petrobras increases jet fuel prices sharply by more than 54%, triggering airfares rises and operational adjustments across the aviation sector. For travellers planning trips within Brazil or connecting through South America’s largest economy, understanding how this jet fuel hike in Brazil reshapes flight pricing, route availability, airline capacity and travel planning has never been more important. This surge in aviation fuel costs is one of the most consequential developments for passengers, travel managers, tourism professionals and holidaymakers navigating Brazil’s travel market in the year ahead.

Why Cetane Pricing Matters for Air Travel

Jet fuel — known officially as aviation kerosene (QAV) — is the lifeblood of any airline, accounting for almost half of operating costs in Brazil after the price surge. Petrol and energy prices move quickly with global markets, and when crude oil prices rise, the price of jet fuel follows. In early April 2026, Petrobras — Brazil’s state‑controlled oil producer — confirmed a 54.8% increase in the price of jet fuel sold to distributors. This spike comes amid elevated global energy prices and geopolitical tensions, pushing aviation fuel costs sharply upward. Airlines warn that this increase will inevitably cascade into higher flight costs and altered travel dynamics for passengers flying within and from Brazil.

Immediate Effects on Flight Prices and Ticketing

Passengers flying in and out of Brazil should prepare for possible airfare rises. Industry analysts estimate that airlines will need to adjust ticket prices several percentage points higher to cover increased fuel expenses, possibly adding between 8% and 15% to average fares in upcoming booking windows. This means that travellers booking flights for domestic holidays, international business travel or regional layovers may find themselves paying more than previously budgeted as airlines recalibrate pricing. Brazil’s largest carriers and regional airlines alike are bracing for these added costs, signalling a new pricing era for the market.

Airlines Respond with Capacity and Route Adjustments

Airlines are not just responding with fare hikes. Major carriers are also reassessing their flight schedules and network planning. With fuel suddenly representing nearly 45% of total operating costs, some carriers may reduce less profitable routes or trim frequency on under‑performing lines. For travellers planning multi‑city journeys in Brazil — for instance from São Paulo to Manaus, or Rio de Janeiro to Porto Alegre — changes in capacity could mean fewer options or less flexibility on timing. Those planning longer stays in smaller cities or remote regions should consider booking earlier or exploring alternative transport modes to maintain travel comfort and value.

Brazil’s Government and Regulatory Response

In response to industry concerns, Brazil’s Ministry of Ports and Airports is exploring tax relief measures to soften the blow of soaring fuel prices. Proposals include temporary reductions in certain federal fuel taxes and expedited refunds of state levies on aviation fuel. While these measures could ease airline financial pressure, their implementation depends on political and legislative timelines, so travelers should not count on immediate relief. From a travel planning perspective, this means that higher flight costs could remain in place for months before any regulatory action takes effect.

Strategic Travel Planning Under New Cost Pressures

Travel managers, corporate planners and frequent flyers need to rethink strategies for navigating the new landscape. For organisations with heavy travel schedules, locking in block‑seat deals and securing early bookings can mitigate fare volatility. Leisure travellers planning Brazilian vacations — from the Amazon rainforest to Rio’s beaches — should also book well in advance to secure favourable pricing before new fare adjustments take hold. In some cases, corporate clients may consider virtual meetings instead of short‑haul trips to reduce travel expense exposure in the wake of higher fuel and flight costs.

Ripple Effects Across Tourism and Hospitality

Higher travel costs do not stop at the cost of planes. When flights become more expensive, overall travel demand can soften, affecting hotel occupancy, tour bookings and regional tourism flows. Brazil’s tourism economy — from luxury resorts in Bahia to eco‑lodges in the Pantanal — could feel the impact if travellers reduce trip frequency or shorten stays. Local tourism businesses should prepare promotional campaigns and package deals that highlight value‑added experiences, balancing cost with high‑quality travel opportunities.

What This Means for International Travellers

International passengers connecting through Brazil or flying between South America and destinations in North America, Europe or Asia will also see effects. Sharp fuel cost increases have global implications, often leading airlines to reprice international routes to maintain profitability. Travellers flying transcontinental routes that include Brazilian legs should factor in potential price shifts and consider alternative hubs or carriers if cost pressures significantly increase. Early ticket locking and flexible cancellation options can be vital for managing travel budgets in a volatile pricing environment.

Consumer Tips on Navigating the New Pricing Climate

In this era of elevated jet fuel prices, travellers can take steps to navigate the situation effectively. Comparing flight options across airlines and booking in advance remain key tactics. Travel insurance that covers price changes or cancellation flexibility becomes more valuable when airfare unpredictability rises. Frequent flyers should also review loyalty programme options that can offer seat upgrades or fare discounts when fuel surcharges weigh heavily on published ticket prices. Knowledgeable travel planning ensures better value even when base costs climb.

The Role of Sustainable Aviation Fuel and Future Trends

Longer term, the aviation industry and governments worldwide — including Brazil — are increasingly eyeing alternatives like sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) to reduce dependency on traditional jet fuel and the associated price volatility tied to crude oil markets. While SAF remains more costly and less widespread today, it represents a significant future opportunity to stabilise operating costs and lessen environmental impacts. For the savvy traveller, staying informed about sustainability developments in aviation can signal future changes in travel cost structures and flight options.

Planning Through Volatility: Travel in 2026

As 2026 unfolds, price volatility driven by international geopolitical tensions and energy market fluctuations underscores the need for adaptive travel strategies. In Brazil, the jet fuel price hike highlights how macroeconomic and energy sector decisions directly influence the travel experience. Travellers should stay updated on airline announcements, regulatory maneuvers, and fuel pricing trends, using this insight to inform itinerary choices, budgeting and travel timing. A proactive approach ensures continued enjoyment of travel opportunities — even in a shifting cost environment.

title: Studi Kelayakan Pabrik Bioavtur, Membelah Langit Energi Indonesia Modern
description:
Dalam studi kasus tersebut, mahasiswa diminta bertindak sebagai tim Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) yang harus menentukan teknologi terbaik untuk pabrik bioavtur berkapasitas 50.000 ton per tahun di kawasan industri Kendal, Jawa Tengah.
Tidak hanya itu, bioavtur hasil HEFA juga langsung memenuhi spesifikasi internasional untuk penerbangan, sehingga berpotensi diterima oleh maskapai-maskapai global.
Untuk menghasilkan 50.000 ton bioavtur per tahun, pabrik membutuhkan sekitar 62.500 ton minyak jelantah, atau setara hampir 190 ton per hari.
Dengan harga jual bioavtur sebesar Rp18 juta per ton, potensi pendapatan pabrik mencapai Rp900 miliar per tahun.
Mereka belajar menghitung neraca massa dan energi, memilih teknologi, menyusun layout pabrik, mengevaluasi risiko, hingga berbicara dalam bahasa investasi global.
text:
Di tengah tuntutan dunia untuk menekan emisi karbon dan menghadirkan energi yang lebih bersih, sebuah gagasan besar lahir dari ruang-ruang akademik Program Studi Sarjana Terapan Teknologi Rekayasa Kimia Industri (TRKI) Vokasi Universitas Diponegoro. Melalui kajian studi kasus yang disusun secara visioner oleh Dr. Mohamad Endy Julianto dan Yusuf Ma’rifat Fajar Azis, ST, MT, mahasiswa diajak memasuki dunia nyata industri masa depan: merancang pabrik bioavtur berbasis minyak jelantah yang bukan hanya layak secara teknis, tetapi juga menguntungkan, aman, dan berkelas internasional.

Kajian ini berangkat dari tantangan besar Indonesia. Pemerintah menargetkan penurunan emisi sektor transportasi udara sebesar 30% pada tahun 2040. Di saat yang sama, kebutuhan avtur nasional terus meningkat. Di sinilah minyak jelantah—yang selama ini kerap dipandang sebagai limbah—berubah menjadi peluang emas. Dengan pendekatan rekayasa proses, limbah rumah tangga dan industri kuliner dapat disulap menjadi Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), bioavtur modern yang lebih ramah lingkungan dan menjadi masa depan industri penerbangan dunia.

Dalam studi kasus tersebut, mahasiswa diminta bertindak sebagai tim Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) yang harus menentukan teknologi terbaik untuk pabrik bioavtur berkapasitas 50.000 ton per tahun di kawasan industri Kendal, Jawa Tengah. Dua alternatif teknologi dibandingkan secara tajam: Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids (HEFA) dan Catalytic Pyrolysis.

Hasilnya sangat menarik. Meskipun teknologi HEFA membutuhkan investasi lebih besar, yakni Rp950 miliar, teknologi ini mampu memberikan yield produk hingga 80%, jauh di atas Catalytic Pyrolysis yang hanya 65%. Tidak hanya itu, bioavtur hasil HEFA juga langsung memenuhi spesifikasi internasional untuk penerbangan, sehingga berpotensi diterima oleh maskapai-maskapai global. Dari sisi emisi, HEFA pun lebih unggul karena menghasilkan jejak karbon yang lebih rendah dan lebih selaras dengan agenda transisi energi dunia.

Lebih memukau lagi ketika angka-angka ekonomi mulai berbicara. Untuk menghasilkan 50.000 ton bioavtur per tahun, pabrik membutuhkan sekitar 62.500 ton minyak jelantah, atau setara hampir 190 ton per hari. Dengan harga jual bioavtur sebesar Rp18 juta per ton, potensi pendapatan pabrik mencapai Rp900 miliar per tahun. Setelah dikurangi biaya bahan baku dan operasional, teknologi HEFA masih mampu menghasilkan laba kotor sekitar Rp280 miliar per tahun.

Angka tersebut menjadikan proyek ini sangat menarik di mata investor. Payback period teknologi HEFA tercatat hanya sekitar 3,39 tahun—jauh di bawah batas maksimal investor yaitu 6 tahun. Artinya, modal dapat kembali dalam waktu relatif singkat, sementara keuntungan jangka panjang tetap sangat besar. Bahkan dibandingkan teknologi Catalytic Pyrolysis yang membutuhkan investasi lebih rendah, HEFA tetap unggul karena menghasilkan keuntungan lebih tinggi, kualitas produk lebih baik, dan peluang pasar internasional yang jauh lebih luas.

Namun kajian ini tidak berhenti pada hitungan laba semata. Dr. Mohamad Endy Julianto dan Yusuf Ma’rifat Fajar Azis juga menempatkan keselamatan proses sebagai jantung perancangan pabrik. Teknologi HEFA memang membawa risiko besar karena menggunakan hidrogen pada tekanan 50 bar dan suhu 350°C. Risiko kebocoran hidrogen, ledakan reaktor, runaway reaction, hingga kegagalan pasokan bahan baku menjadi perhatian utama.

Karena itu, mahasiswa dilatih berpikir layaknya engineer profesional kelas dunia melalui pendekatan HAZOP dan LOPA. Setiap potensi bahaya dipetakan, dianalisis, lalu diberikan lapisan perlindungan. Reaktor harus dilengkapi Safety Instrumented System (SIS), Emergency Shutdown (ESD), relief valve menuju flare, fire and gas detector, hingga sistem isolasi otomatis jika terjadi kebocoran. Area penyimpanan minyak jelantah, unit hidrogen, dan reaktor pun harus dipisahkan secara ketat sesuai standar internasional API, NFPA, dan OSHA.

Dari sinilah terlihat bahwa pembelajaran di TRKI Vokasi Undip bukan sekadar menghafal teori, melainkan melatih mahasiswa menghadapi tantangan industri yang sesungguhnya. Mereka belajar menghitung neraca massa dan energi, memilih teknologi, menyusun layout pabrik, mengevaluasi risiko, hingga berbicara dalam bahasa investasi global.

Kajian ini menjadi bukti bahwa kampus vokasi mampu melahirkan gagasan besar yang relevan dengan masa depan Indonesia. Dari minyak jelantah yang sering dianggap tak bernilai, lahirlah visi baru tentang langit Indonesia yang lebih hijau, industri yang lebih berkelanjutan, dan generasi engineer yang siap bersaing di panggung dunia. Bersama Dr. Mohamad Endy Julianto dan Yusuf Ma’rifat Fajar Azis, TRKI Vokasi Undip sedang menunjukkan bahwa masa depan energi tidak hanya dibayangkan—tetapi sedang dirancang, dihitung, dan dipersiapkan mulai hari ini.

Stell dir vor, du sitzt im Flugzeug und schaust aus dem Fenster: American Airlines Group dominiert den US-Himmel mit Tausenden Flügen täglich. Aber als Anleger fragst du dich: Lohnt sich die Aktie (ISIN: US02376R1023, Nasdaq, USD) jetzt? Die Branche ist volatil, doch genau hier lauern Chancen für mutige Investoren wie dich aus Europa oder den USA.

Du kennst die Szene: Treibstoffpreise schwanken, Passagierzahlen boomen post-Pandemie, aber Konkurrenz und Kosten drücken. Wir schauen uns an, warum American Airlines Group trotz allem interessant bleibt. Bleib dran, ich zeige dir die Fakten.

Stand: 05.04.2026

von Lukas Berger, Börsenredakteur: American Airlines Group fliegt als Marktführer durch stürmische Lüfte – hier die Essenz für clevere Anleger.

Das Geschäftsmodell: So verdient American Airlines ihr Geld

American Airlines Group ist der Mutterkonzern hinter der Marke American Airlines, der weltweit größten Airline nach Passagierkilometern. Du investierst in eine Holding, die Passagierflüge, Fracht und Loyalitätsprogramme bündelt. Der Kern: Netzwerk aus Hub-and-Spoke-Modell mit starken Knotenpunkten wie Dallas/Fort Worth und Miami.

Du fragst dich, wie das Geld fließt? Haupteinnahmen kommen aus Ticketverkäufen, die rund 80 Prozent ausmachen, ergänzt durch Zuschläge für Gepäck oder Sitzplatzreservierungen. AAdvantage, das Vielfliegerprogramm, generiert stabile Einnahmen durch Partnerschaften mit Kreditkartenfirmen – ein echter Cashflow-Treiber für dich als Anleger.

Die Flotte umfasst über 900 Flugzeuge, darunter effiziente Boeing 737 und Airbus A320. Du profitierst von Skaleneffekten: Je mehr Passagiere, desto niedriger die Kosten pro Sitzkilometer. Aber Achtung: Leasingkosten und Wartung fressen Margen, wenn Auslastung nachlässt.

Insgesamt ist das Modell robust, solange Reisen boomen. Für dich als europäischen Investor bedeutet das: Exposition zu US-Wirtschaftswachstum ohne Währungsrisiko, wenn du in USD handelst.

Branchentreiber: Was treibt die Airline-Branche voran

Die Airline-Branche lebt von Nachfragezyklen. Du siehst aktuell einen Boom: Reisen normalisieren sich, Business-Trips kehren zurück. Leisure-Reisen aus Europa in die USA boomen – perfekt für dich als Investor in Frankfurt oder New York.

Treibstoffpreise sind der größte Hebel: Sie machen bis zu 30 Prozent der Kosten aus. Sinkende Ölpreise pushen Gewinne, steigende drücken. Nachhaltigkeit wird zum Treiber: Airlines investieren in SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel), um regulatorischen Druck zu kontern.

Digitalisierung hilft: Apps für Check-in und Upselling steigern Einnahmen pro Passagier. Für dich relevant: Kapazitätsengpässe durch Lieferverzögerungen bei Boeing und Airbus machen American Airlines attraktiv, da sie bestehende Flotten effizient nutzt.

Geopolitik spielt mit: Weniger Fernreisen bei Konflikten, aber starke Domestic-Nachfrage in den USA puffert. Du solltest auf Rezessionssignale achten – Airlines sind Frühindikatoren.

Analystenstimmen: Was sagen die Experten?

Renommierte Banken beobachten American Airlines Group genau. Viele Analysten sehen Potenzial in der Erholung, betonen aber Kostendisziplin. Große Häuser wie JPMorgan oder Barclays halten die Aktie im Blick, mit Fokus auf Flottenmodernisierung und Schuldenabbau.

Du findest vielfältige Einschätzungen: Einige raten zum Halten, da Margen sich erholen könnten, andere warnen vor Konkurrenzdruck. Keine einheitliche Kaufwelle, aber optimistische Szenarien bei stabilen Treibstoffpreisen. Das Bild ist nuanciert – ideal für dich, um selbst abzuwägen.

Research-Häuser heben die starke Marktposition hervor. Für europäische Anleger: Die Aktie bietet Yield durch Dividendenpotenzial, sobald Cashflow stabil ist. Achte auf Updates von Morningstar oder Seeking Alpha-Zusammenfassungen.

Deine Investorenrelevanz: Warum AAL für Europa und USA passt

Als Anleger aus Europa oder den USA bist du nah am Geschehen. American Airlines verbindet Frankfurt mit Dallas direkt – du profitierst von Transatlantik-Boom. Die Aktie ist liquide, perfekt für Portfolios mit US-Exposition.

Du suchst Diversifikation? Airlines korrelieren mit Konsum und GDP-Wachstum. In Zeiten niedriger Zinsen lockt das hohe Beta – Volatilität, aber auch Upside. Für US-Investoren: Steuerliche Vorteile bei Nasdaq-Handel.

Vergleich zu Delta oder United: American hat die größte Flotte, aber höhere Schulden. Du gewinnst durch Netzwerkvorteile in Lateinamerika. Jetzt kaufen? Warte auf Dipps, wenn Öl steigt.

Relevanz heute: Inflation kühlt ab, Reisen bleiben stark. Du solltest auf Earnings achten – Quartalszahlen zeigen Auslastungstrends.

Risiken und offene Fragen: Worauf du achten musst

Risiken lauern überall. Rezession könnte Auslastung killen – Airlines hassen leere Sitze. Du kennst das: 2020 hat die Branche Milliarden verschlungen. Heute: Schuldenberg von der Pandemie bleibt Hürde.

Treibstoff und Arbeitskosten explodieren bei Inflation. Pilotenstreiks oder Lieferkettenprobleme bremsen. Regulatorisch: CO2-Steuern in Europa treffen Transatlantik-Routen hart – du als EU-Anleger spürst das.

Offene Fragen: Wann kommt die Dividende zurück? Flottenumbau schafft Kosten. Konkurrenz von Low-Cost-Carriern wie Spirit drückt Premium-Preise. Du achtest am besten auf Load-Factor und RASM (Revenue per Available Seat Mile).

Trotzdem: Resilienz durch Größe. Du diversifizierst clever, wenn du AAL mit Tech-Aktien mischt.

Ausblick: Worauf du als Nächstes schaust

Der Ausblick? Positiv bei anhaltender Erholung. Du siehst Sommerreiseboom als Katalysator. Strategie: Kostensenkung durch Technik und Partnerschaften wie mit Google Cloud.

Für dich relevant: Nächste Earnings im April könnten Klarheit bringen. Achte auf Guidance zu 2026 – Kapazitätswachstum unter 5 Prozent wäre bullisch.

Langfristig: Nachhaltigkeit und Digitalisierung sichern Zukunft. Du kaufst nicht blind, sondern bei Unterbewertung. Vergleich PE mit Peers: Oft günstiger als Delta.

Fazit: American Airlines Group ist kein Schnäppchen, aber solider Play auf Reisen. Du entscheidest basierend auf Risikobereitschaft – jetzt beobachten, später einsteigen.

text:
StormFisher Hydrogen Ltd. and CarbonLeap B.V. have formed a partnership to support Scope 3 emission reductions in transatlantic maritime logistics. The collaboration links StormFisher’s Renewable Fuels of Non‑Biological Origin certified e‑methanol with CarbonLeap’s system for aggregating cargo‑owner demand to co‑finance low carbon fuel adoption. StormFisher plans to supply e‑methanol produced at its Varennes facility in Québec, where green hydrogen generated through electrolysis will be combined with captured carbon dioxide to produce approximately 70,000 tonnes of e‑methanol annually. The fuel is expected to reduce lifecycle carbon intensity by more than 85 percent compared to conventional marine fuels.

CarbonLeap’s book‑and‑claim model enables cargo owners to claim verified emissions reductions regardless of the vessel or carrier used, addressing challenges associated with multi‑carrier supply chains. Under the partnership, carriers deploy the e‑methanol on selected voyages while CarbonLeap manages verification and allocates emissions benefits to participating cargo owners. The arrangement is intended to provide a cost‑competitive pathway for companies seeking to reduce transport‑related Scope 3 emissions and to expand access to low carbon maritime transport solutions on European and transatlantic trade routes.

text:
Rob Wattelé leidt sinds augustus 2025 Pipelink, de beheerder van een ondergronds pijpleidingennetwerk, dat cruciaal is voor de industrie. Als nieuwe CEO staat hij voor de uitdaging om de “slagaders van de economie” klaar te maken voor de energietransitie, terwijl de druk van stijgende prijzen en internationale concurrentie toeneemt.

Rob Wattelé (42) kent de grootindustrie door en door. Met een master industriële scheikunde en een master maritieme economie combineert hij proceskennis met inzicht in logistieke ketens. Zijn carrière bij Solvay en INEOS Inovyn bracht hem van plantoperaties tot internationale projectteams, waarna hij bij Port of Antwerp-Bruges verantwoordelijk werd voor het chemiesegment.

“Die combinatie van strategische en operationele ervaring heeft me uitstekend voorbereid”, zegt hij. “In de chemie zag ik elke dag hoe afhankelijk bedrijven zijn van betrouwbare pijpleidingen voor grondstoffen en eindproducten. In de haven leerde ik hoe infrastructuur de concurrentiekracht van hele clusters bepaalt. Die twee werelden komen bij Pipelink perfect samen.”

Open pijpleidingnetwerk als kantelpunt

Pipelink is sinds 2017 een dochter van Port of Antwerp-Bruges en kreeg eind 2023 North Sea Port aan boord als minderheidsaandeelhouder. Daarmee vertegenwoordigt het bedrijf de drie grootste Vlaamse havenplatformen. Het beheert leidingen voor klassieke chemische producten zoals propyleen, ethyleen, aceton, fenol, chloor en natriumhydroxide, en is marktleider in niet-gereguleerde moleculen. Maar volgens Wattelé staat het bedrijf op een structureel kantelmoment.

De klassieke point-to-pointverbindingen – één producent, één afnemer – botsen op hun limieten. De industrie heeft schaal nodig, flexibiliteit en vooral kostenvoordelen. “We evolueren van geïsoleerde point-to-pointverbindingen tussen één producent en één afnemer naar echte multi-user- en multi-accessnetwerken. Meerdere bedrijven kunnen tegelijk op dezelfde leiding aansluiten. Dat verlaagt kosten, versnelt investeringen en maakt verduurzaming haalbaar voor de hele sector”, stelt Wattelé.

Die omslag is niet louter technisch, maar economisch. Nieuwe moleculen zoals waterstof, ammoniak of koolstofdioxide vereisen volumes die individuele bedrijven vaak niet kunnen garanderen, terwijl de financiering van infrastructuur steeds moeilijker wordt door druk op de marges en langere investeringscycli. De Europese industrie staat bovendien voor strengere klimaatdoelstellingen en een groeiende concurrentie van importstromen.

Wattelé ziet hierin vooral kansen: “Te midden van die transitie ontstaan enorme mogelijkheden voor innovatieve moleculen zoals CO2, waterstof, ammoniak, methanol en zelfs Sustainable Aviation Fuel.”

Infrastructuur is een hefboom voor een hele keten

Pipelink probeert de investeringsdrempel te verlagen door bedrijven te ondersteunen bij financiering en realisatie, waarbij ook gekeken wordt naar het gebruik van eventuele beschikbare publieke instrumenten. “We creëren complete ecosystemen waarin infrastructuur geen bottleneck meer is, maar een hefboom voor de hele keten – van import via de havens tot afnemers in het hinterland. Door krachten te bundelen – in volumes én investeringen – worden projecten rendabel die voor één partij alleen niet haalbaar zijn.”

Veilig en efficiënt

Wattelé benadrukt dat pijpleidingen, naast spoor en binnenvaart, een strategische rol spelen in de energietransitie en essentieel zijn voor een robuuste industrie. “Ze zijn de veiligste, energiezuinigste, meest betrouwbare en meest kostenefficiënte manier om grote volumes over lange afstanden te vervoeren. Voor de industrie, logistiek en maritieme sector betekent dat lagere transportkosten, minder kapitaalbeslag en een lagere drempel om te vergroenen.”

De strategie van Pipelink staat haarscherp: de grootindustrie ontzorgen door infrastructuur te ontwerpen, te bouwen, te financieren en te beheren. Wattelé: “Je bent alleen succesvol als je de hele keten meekrijgt – van producent tot eindafnemer en van importeur tot hinterland. Bedrijven willen zich focussen op hun core business; wij nemen de infrastructuur voor onze rekening. We ondersteunen bij de financiering en realisatie van pijpleidingprojecten, en nemen het beheer op ons, ook voor de assets van derde partijen.”

De economische logica is helder: wie zoals Pipelink de regie van de infrastructuur in handen neemt, verlaagt de risico’s voor investeerders en versnelt de uitrol van nieuwe waardeketens. Dat is cruciaal in een markt waar de tijdsdruk toeneemt en de concurrentie internationaal is.

ARRRA-corridor als gamechanger

Met North Sea Port als aandeelhouder heeft Pipelink ook een bredere geografische horizon. De ambitie reikt verder dan de Antwerpse havencluster. De duurzame corridor Antwerpen-Rotterdam-Rhine-Ruhr (ARRRA) moet uitgroeien tot een ondergrondse ruggengraat voor de Benelux en het Ruhrgebied.

Wattelé: “We kijken verder dan het havenplatform in Antwerpen. De toekomst ligt in grensoverschrijdende infrastructuur die hele industriële ecosystemen met elkaar verbindt. We willen de modal shift niet enkel bovengronds realiseren via schip, spoor of weg, maar bij uitstek ook ondergronds: veilig, energiezuinig, betrouwbaar en met lage transportkosten op lange termijn.”

Het netwerk van Pipelink is grensoverschrijdend schaalbaar

De versterking van de ARRRA-corridor is van strategisch belang: “Wie de import van low-carbon moleculen wil verzekeren, moet de verbindingen naar het hinterland versterken”, stelt Wattelé. Dat geldt zowel voor waterstof en ammoniak als voor CO₂-afvang en -opslag. De CO₂-backbone in Antwerpen, een joint venture met Fluxys via c-grid Antwerp, vormt een initiële stap binnen het project, maar Wattelé benadrukt dat dit slechts het begin is.

“Het netwerk is grensoverschrijdend schaalbaar en beperkt zich niet tot de ecosystemen van onze aandeelhouders. Wij werken tevens actief binnen de bredere regio Antwerpen-Rotterdam-Rhine-Ruhr en stellen onze expertise en diensten beschikbaar om ontwikkelingen op andere continenten te ondersteunen. Dit kan op termijn bijdragen aan de import van koolstofarme producten naar de Europese Unie.”

De succescriteria voor Pipelink zijn concreet: nieuwe gebruikers aansluiten, ontzorgen van de industrie waar mogelijk, groei realiseren in het volume duurzame moleculen en kruisverbindingen mogelijk maken die de havengrenzen overstijgen. Het zijn tastbare indicatoren in een sector waar veel plannen vaak te lang op de tekentafel blijven liggen.

Pipelink houdt aandacht op ontzorging van de traditionele industrie

“Infrastructuur is geen bijzaak. Pijpleidingen zijn de ondergrondse slagaders die de chemie van morgen mogelijk maken. Wie wil meespelen in de internationale concurrentie, moet vandaag investeren in ondergrondse connectiviteit. We houden de aandacht op ontzorging van de traditionele industrie en willen futureproof zijn in de transitie. Die focus versterkt niet alleen de concurrentiepositie van de ARRRA-regio, maar ondersteunt ook de bredere Europese transitie”, besluit Wattelé.

Maar de knoop werd doorgehakt in 2019.” En vervolgens: jarenlang niks.
We hadden veel te weinig mensen, te weinig budget, niet de juiste expertise.
Nooit gedacht: we stoppen ermee en concentreren ons op de handel.
Zo breidt marktleider Neste zijn fabriek in Rotterdam uit naar 2,7 miljoen ton per jaar en wil het eveneens Amsterdamse Power2x een fabriek voor synthetische kerosine bouwen.
text:
Het is spitsuur aan de koffiebar van SkyNRG, in het voormalige postkantoor bij de Nieuwmarkt waar Amsterdammers in het hartje van de stad ooit hun postzegels kochten. Nu stromen er – op papier – jaarlijks honderdduizenden tonnen biokerosine door de kantoren.

SkyNRG is een van de grootste handelaren in alternatieve vliegtuigbrandstof, met meer dan vijftig maatschappijen op de klantenlijst. KLM voorop, die nu 2 procent van haar brandstofbehoefte uit duurzamere bron tankt. Die ‘sustainable aviation fuel’ (SAF, duurzamere vliegtuigbrandstof) scheelt 80 tot 90 procent CO2-uitstoot.

Over twee jaar stroomt SkyNRG-kerosine ook echt. Vanuit een fabriek in Delfzijl waaraan sinds kort wordt gebouwd, nadat de Amsterdamse haven eerder was afgevallen. Jaarlijks 100.000 ton uit afgewerkt vet, waarvan het merendeel voor aandeelhouder KLM. Het is de droom van Maarten van Dijk, die het bedrijf in 2009 met partners oprichtte. Maar wel een droom met wachtlijst.

Wanneer dachten jullie: we handelen in het spul, maar we kunnen het ook zelf gaan maken?

“In 2016 had ik het eerste plannetje. In 2017 hebben we de eerste mensen aangenomen en een klein beetje geld opgehaald. Maar de knoop werd doorgehakt in 2019.”

En vervolgens: jarenlang niks.

“We dachten: in drie, vier jaar kan dat ding er staan. Maar steeds gebeurden er dingen: de PAS-affaire, stikstofcrisis, corona. De bouwkosten gingen door het dak, de Europese regels voor het bijmengen van SAF veranderden.”

“We wisten gewoon niet zo goed wat we deden. We hadden veel te weinig mensen, te weinig budget, niet de juiste expertise. We hebben alles gewoon volledig verkeerd ingeschat. Dat is mijn schuld. Dat hebben mensen toen ook tegen me gezegd. Fluor, Shell en Akzo zaten in onze adviesraad en zeiden: bij een project van deze omvang heb je alleen al voor de voorbereiding een team nodig van 20, 25 mensen. Goed. Dus wij doen er twee. Ik heb gewoon niet geluisterd.”

Wanneer kwam de klif in zicht?

“Mijn idee was dat wíj die fabriek ontwikkelden, iemand anders hem voor ons zou draaien en wij dan de brandstof zouden krijgen. Dat was best een dom idee. Geen enkele uitbater neemt het risico met nieuwe technologie om vervolgens ook nog eens de productie af te staan.”

“We moesten het dus zelf doen. Maar dat konden onze toenmalige aandeelhouders, KLM en particuliere investeerders, niet behappen. Dus was ik niet bezig een nieuwe fabriek te bouwen, maar een nieuw bedrijf. Met nieuwe aandeelhouders die geld meebrachten. Uiteindelijk stapte Macquarie in met 175 miljoen euro en APG (de belegger van pensioenfonds ABP, red.) met 250 miljoen. Daarna konden we verder.”

Al dat oponthoud was koren op de molen van critici: zie je wel, het lukt niet met SAF.

“We hebben onszelf in de voet geschoten door er zo lang over te doen, in een wereld die toch al kritisch tegenover de verduurzaming van de luchtvaart staat. Maar we hebben altijd doorgezet. Nooit gedacht: we stoppen ermee en concentreren ons op de handel. Er moet gewoon meer SAF komen en wij moeten daar het voorbeeld in geven.”

Het helpt dan niet mee dat jullie vanaf 2028 jaarlijks 100.000 ton duurzame kerosine produceren, terwijl KLM een veelvoud daarvan nodig heeft om in 2030 wereldwijd 10 procent SAF te tanken.

“Driekwart van onze productie gaat straks naar KLM. Dat is 2,5 procent van haar brandstofbehoefte. Dus moeten ze het overal kopen, in de hele wereld, bij verschillende producenten. Ze mengen nu 4,6 procent SAF bij. Dat levert een solide basis voor groei. Het is zo makkelijk om daar kritiek op te hebben en meteen ‘greenwashing’ te roepen: ze doen het gewoon. Zo zijn er meer in de wereld.”

Jullie grondstof bestaat, net als bij andere producenten, uit gebruikte oliën en afval uit de voedingsindustrie. Jullie hadden ook prachtige plannen, met houtsnippers van omgehakte bomen bijvoorbeeld.

“Als idee was het hartstikke mooi, maar die hoeveelheid is te klein en het is moeilijk te combineren met de grote stroom grondstoffen uit de voedingsindustrie.”

Ook de plas afgewerkt frituurvet is bij lange na niet genoeg.

“Het is meer dan frituurvet alleen. Er is in de EU een hele lijst producten uit de voedingsindustrie die gebruikt kunnen worden. Wij zetten bij sommige vraagtekens. Afval van de palmolie-industrie, bijvoorbeeld. Dat kan je niet meer eten, maar wel raffineren. Dan ben je volgens Europa hartstikke duurzaam bezig.”

“Maar het is natuurlijk heel makkelijk om net even iets meer te morsen. Het risico op fraude in de palmolieketen is zo groot, dat wij het niet verhandelen. Dat heeft ons weleens een Aziatische luchtvaartmaatschappij gekost.”

Dat beperkt het aanbod nog verder. Terwijl de behoefte aan SAF vele malen groter is dan het aanbod.

“Daarom werken we ook aan alternatieven. We zetten met partners een fabriek op voor synthetische kerosine in Zweden, Skykraft, waarbij de benodigde stroom voor de productie van waterstof wordt opgewekt met waterkracht en de benodigde CO2 afkomstig is uit de papierindustrie.”

“En we werken met Boeing aan een fabriek in de Amerikaanse staat Washington, waar we SAF produceren met biogas uit afvalbergen. Beide openen rond 2030 met ongeveer dezelfde capaciteit als de fabriek in Delfzijl: 100.000 ton per jaar.”

Volgens luchtvaartorganisatie Iata is vorig jaar wereldwijd 1,9 miljoen ton SAF geproduceerd, 0,6 procent van wat de mondiale luchtvaartsector nodig heeft. Er komt wel nieuwe productiecapaciteit bij. Zo breidt marktleider Neste zijn fabriek in Rotterdam uit naar 2,7 miljoen ton per jaar en wil het eveneens Amsterdamse Power2x een fabriek voor synthetische kerosine bouwen.

Maar er verdwijnt nog meer. Shell en BP hebben de stekker uit hun biokerosinefabrieken in Rotterdam getrokken. En SkyNRG’s eigen Synkeroproject voor synthetische kerosine in Amsterdam staat in de wachtkamer omdat de businesscase niet rondkomt vanwege een tekort aan groene waterstof.

“Dat is ontzettend jammer,” zegt Van Dijk. “Ook voor het imago van de alternatieve brandstofmarkt. Maar je vindt geen geld voor zulke enorme investeringen als de vraag en de politieke omgeving nog te onzeker zijn, ook niet als je Shell bent. Dat zal veranderen, maar het gaat langzaam. Ik maak me meer zorgen over sommige andere oliereuzen, Amerikaanse voorop, die vanwege de politieke wind in de VS plots een andere koers varen.”

“SAF zit in Brussel nog te veel aan de duurzaamheidskant. Het opwekken van eigen energiestromen is minstens even belangrijk. Daarom begrijp ik ook niet zo goed dat er niet veel meer steun vanuit overheden voor bioraffinaderijen is. Gebruik een deel van de opbrengst uit het emissiehandelssysteem ervoor.”

“Voor onze energiebehoefte zijn eigen brandstoffabrieken cruciaal. We weten hoe gevoelig de aanvoer van ruwe olie en olieproducten is, we maken het nu mee. Reden te meer om veel actiever te kijken naar alternatieven. Daarbij zijn ook biokerosine en synthetische brandstof onontbeerlijk. Hoeveel andere opties heb je in Europa om aan de eigen energiezekerheid te werken?”

Biokerosine is nu drie keer zo duur als fossiele brandstof, de synthetische variant een factor twaalf. Zal dat ooit veranderen?

“Als de productie toeneemt, zullen de kosten en de prijzen dalen. Van de EU moet na 2030 synthetische kerosine worden bijgemengd. Dat zal de productie aanjagen. Maar het wordt nooit de prijs van fossiele kerosine. We gaan hoe dan ook meer betalen om te vliegen en dat is een goede bijkomstigheid. Vliegreizigers moeten ook beter gaan nadenken over hun reis.”

title: Australia faces fuel crisis; Canegrowers pushes E10 solution - Queensland Country Life
description:
Australia has spent years moving towards cheaper, imported fuel, while our own domestic capacity has been left largely untapped.
That worked well enough when global supply chains were stable.
We're now seeing the consequences play out - not just at the bowser, but right through the supply chain.
We're also leading an industry-wide supply chain taskforce, bringing together key players from across the sugar industry to assess the situation and identify practical responses.
There are also real opportunities in biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel, particularly for regional Australia.
text:
If you've filled up lately, you don't need to be told something's wrong.

Prices are up, availability is tightening, and in some areas fuel is already hard to find.

That's not just frustrating - for many regional businesses and farming operations, it's a real concern heading into the busy part of the year.

And while global conflict has brought the issue to a head, the reality is this didn't come out of nowhere.

Australia has spent years moving towards cheaper, imported fuel, while our own domestic capacity has been left largely untapped.

That worked well enough when global supply chains were stable. It's a different story when they're not.

We're now seeing the consequences play out - not just at the bowser, but right through the supply chain.

Fuel is a core input for agriculture.

When prices rise or supply becomes uncertain, it flows straight through to planting, harvesting and transport.

It also flows through to freight, food prices and the cost of doing business more broadly.

That's why Canegrowers has been working closely with the National Farmers' Federation, Queensland Farmers' Federation, and both State and Federal governments to make sure the risks facing agriculture are clearly understood.

We're also leading an industry-wide supply chain taskforce, bringing together key players from across the sugar industry to assess the situation and identify practical responses.

But while managing the immediate pressure is critical, we can't ignore how we got here.

Australia is not short of fuel options.

We have the capacity to produce more here at home - particularly through ethanol, where a significant share of production capacity is currently sitting idle.

That's why Canegrowers is calling for a compulsory national E10 mandate - ensuring up to 10 per cent of Australia's fuel is produced domestically, while creating the market certainty needed to drive investment in local production.

Every litre produced locally is one less litre we need to import, reducing our exposure when global markets tighten.

There are also real opportunities in biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel, particularly for regional Australia.

None of this will happen without clear policy direction and investment.

Owen Menkens - Canegrowers chairman

text:
Financial Challenges and Market Uncertainty

Archer Aviation, once heralded as a leading innovator in the electric air taxi sector, is now facing significant obstacles as investor enthusiasm for the industry wanes. The company’s stock has fallen sharply, declining 62% from its peak in 2025, reflecting growing skepticism toward high-risk, pre-revenue technology ventures. Despite achieving full compliance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements for its Midnight aircraft, Archer remains pre-revenue and continues to incur substantial losses. In 2025 alone, the company reported an operating loss of $729 million and has resorted to diluting shareholder equity to maintain its operations. While Archer is actively pursuing the launch of air taxi networks in key urban markets such as New York, Florida, and Texas, the timeline and ultimate viability of these initiatives remain uncertain amid the challenging financial landscape.

Industry Risks and Legal Disputes

The air taxi industry is widely regarded as a potential disruptor of urban transportation, yet it remains fraught with considerable risk. Archer’s ongoing cash burn and absence of revenue highlight the difficulties faced by startups attempting to commercialize advanced aviation technologies. These struggles mirror broader challenges within the sector, as investor sentiment shifts away from speculative and capital-intensive enterprises.

Adding to Archer’s operational and financial pressures is a prominent legal dispute with rival Joby Aviation. Archer has filed a counterclaim accusing Joby of fraud, alleging that Joby concealed ties to Chinese entities in order to secure U.S. government contracts. This legal confrontation threatens to divert critical resources and management focus away from Archer’s core mission of developing and deploying air taxis. The dispute has the potential to weaken Archer’s market position and further erode investor confidence. Market reactions to the lawsuit have been mixed; some investors express concern that the legal battle may distract from Archer’s primary business objectives, while others view the action as a necessary defense of the company’s interests. The case has also intensified scrutiny of Joby’s operations, potentially influencing investor sentiment toward both companies.

Outlook and Future Prospects

Archer Aviation remains committed to advancing its regulatory efforts and launching air taxi networks in New York, Florida, and Texas. However, the company’s future is clouded by ongoing financial losses, shareholder dilution, and the distractions posed by its legal dispute with Joby. The resolution of these regulatory and legal challenges will be critical in shaping Archer’s trajectory within the evolving air taxi market.

description:
Government actions in Europe are triggering hidden travel deals in 2026.
Public service obligation (PSO) routes, like those in Scotland, offer subsidised budget flights to remote destinations, with the Highland Council heavily supporting services, making them affordable.
By early April 2026 a cluster of policies had converged to form hidden travel deals.

By booking in April for summer 2026 travel, the new cost can be evaded.
text:
Government actions in Europe are triggering hidden travel deals in 2026. Tax cuts, subsidised flights, and changes in travel authorisation rules are shaping the aviation landscape. Starting April 2026, the German government reduced air traffic tax, lowering fares for short, medium, and long-haul flights. These tax-driven reductions are hidden deals that passengers unknowingly benefit from by booking early. Public service obligation (PSO) routes, like those in Scotland, offer subsidised budget flights to remote destinations, with the Highland Council heavily supporting services, making them affordable. The EU PSO framework allows member states to subsidise vital routes, connecting regions to hubs. The ETIAS system, scheduled for late 2026, creates a fee-free window for travellers booking before it begins. The UK Department for Transport ensures PSOs protect regional services, offering discounted travel to remote areas. These government-driven initiatives highlight the importance of monitoring official sources for policy-driven savings, as travellers who plan ahead can secure deals far beyond traditional marketing strategies. Monitoring official announcements is key to leveraging regulatory advantages and unlocking affordable journeys.

The cost of flying was reshaped by a series of government decisions. By early April 2026 a cluster of policies had converged to form hidden travel deals. Unlike commercial promotions, these deals were created through taxation policy, subsidies and regulations. How official moves affect passengers is explained in this report using verified sources, a third‑person perspective and passive voice. Tax cuts are described first, public service routes are examined next and guidance and comparative programmes are considered last. It will be seen by the reader that meaningful deals often have their origin in government offices rather than marketing departments.

Aviation Tax Cut Creates Early Savings

The German Federal Government decided that the air traffic tax would be reduced from 1 July 2026. The cabinet stated that the levy on short flights would drop to around 13 EUR, the medium rate to about 33 EUR and the long‑haul rate to roughly 59 EUR[1]. The savings could be passed to passengers at the airlines’ discretion[1]. Because fares are set months ahead, pricing from April 2026 onward was influenced by lower tax expectations. Tickets purchased in early April for travel after July reflected the coming reduction. This change operated as a hidden deal because it was not marketed as such. Passengers booking around 4 April observed softer prices.

Scottish Public Service Flights Offer Subsidised Seats

Public service obligation (PSO) routes are designed so that air connections are guaranteed where commercial services would not survive. PSOs may be imposed by governments on vital routes and operation may be limited to a single airline while compensation is provided[2]. Such a PSO is administered by the Highland Council between Wick John O’Groats and Aberdeen. In February 2026 it was announced that tickets covering 1 April – 14 August 2026 would go on sale with a £7.50 per‑leg price rise[3]. The route is subsidised by Transport Scotland and the council[4], keeping fares lower than would otherwise be possible. Ticket sales opened just before 4 April and early bookings captured the benefit. For travellers bound for northern Scotland an affordable option was thus provided.

European Framework for Public Service Obligations

Across Europe, a broader framework for subsidised air travel is formed by PSOs. Routes may be designated as essential and operators may be compensated by member states under Regulation 1008/2008[2]. All PSO announcements, modifications or tenders must be published in the Official Journal of the European Union[2]. When a new PSO is declared or renewed, discounted seats become available. Remote regions are connected to hubs through PSOs and operation at a loss is covered by the government. Early booking can be made by travellers who monitor the Official Journal so that benefit can be gained from the subsidies.

Upcoming Travel Authorisation Brings Timing Advantage

The European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) is scheduled to begin in the last quarter of 2026[5]. No action needs to be taken by travellers yet, but once operational a fee will be charged for authorisation. Because the start date is known, trips can be planned before the system begins so that the fee is avoided. By booking in April for summer 2026 travel, the new cost can be evaded. This timing advantage is a deal created by regulation. Awareness of such changes should be maintained so that hidden benefits can be secured.

UK Guidance on Subsidised Routes

The United Kingdom retained Regulation 1008/2008 in domestic law. Department for Transport guidance from December 2023 explains that PSO tenders must be advertised in the London, Edinburgh and Belfast Gazettes for at least two months[6] while aiming to protect regional connectivity and minimise market distortions and emissions. This framework means subsidised routes may appear without much publicity. By monitoring official gazettes, the tendering of a PSO can be identified and seats can be booked early. Affordable journeys can thus be opened up at short notice by government decisions. The guidance contributes to the understanding that public policy is a source of travel bargains.

Essential Air Service: A Comparative Glimpse

Outside Europe, context is provided by the U.S. Essential Air Service programme. It is explained by the U.S. Department of Transportation that minimum flight frequencies are established and carriers are compensated under EAS to ensure that access is maintained by small communities[7]. Although the programme pertains to the United States, it illustrates how public subsidies create affordable flights where market forces would not sustain them. That Europe’s PSO schemes are part of a wider global practice is shown by the existence of EAS. An appreciation of the universal role of government in aviation can be held by travellers who understand that similar systems are operated by other countries. This comparative glimpse underscores the broader narrative: that official policies, not corporate promotions, often underpin the best deals.

Convergence of Policies Around 4 April 2026

By early April 2026 several of the aforementioned policies were aligning. Fares had begun to be lowered by the upcoming reduction of the German air traffic tax, PSO seats were put on sale by the Highland Council from 1 April and an incentive to travel beforehand was created by the ETIAS start date. The UK’s PSO guidance remained in place, and the broader European framework continued to see tenders. A period in which multiple government‑driven savings were accessible was produced by the convergence of these measures around 4 April. Advantages were inadvertently being taken by passengers booking then through a combination of fiscal relief, public subsidies and regulatory timing. The early‑April window thus stands as a case study in policy‑induced deals.

Looking Ahead: Anticipated Changes and Opportunities

Government policies are not left standing still. New deals may be generated by future adjustments to aviation taxes, expansions of PSO networks or changes in travel authorisation rules. If Germany’s tax cut is emulated by other countries, additional tax‑driven reductions could occur. Openings may be presented for travellers who book at the outset when PSO contracts in France, Italy and Ireland come up for renewal. Another deadline that may be used to avoid fees will be created by the rollout of the Entry/Exit System. Therefore, official announcements, gazettes and regulatory timelines should continue to be monitored by observant travellers. By aligning travel plans with policy changes, savings exceeding those offered through commercial channels can be secured. Further ahead, climate and digital policies may alter the aviation landscape. Proposals to mandate sustainable aviation fuel and to adjust EU Emissions Trading System allowances could add or subtract costs; by watching the legislative timetable, travellers may once again align bookings with cost dips. Similarly, revisions to slot allocation rules and rail–air connectivity initiatives could shift capacity and create new promotional windows. An attentive public can leverage these transitions just as the 2026 tax and PSO measures were leveraged. Monitoring the policy debate becomes part of the travel planning ritual.
